exactness_argument.base: D4 is the k4c400 experiment's frozen base: the pinned oracle checked its header and table, its index and layout digests are reproduced by every process of both binaries, every rank process reproduces the frozen table, and every recovered scalar replays [d]G = Q in the oracle
exactness_argument.producers: R1. **A constant reduce shift at n = 83** (`fmul`, `fsqr`). The parent's `fast_field::mul` and `fast_field::sqr` take the field degree `n`, the mask `2^n - 1` and the tail `t = irr - z^n` as runtime arguments, so the two folds of `reduce` (`h = (lo >> n) | (hi << (128 - n))`, `ht >> n`, `& mask`) shift by a value the compiler cannot see even after inlining (`gf.n` is a field of a struct read from memory). R1 adds, at the head of `fmul` and of `fsqr`, if gf.n == 83 { return unsafe { fast_field::mul(83, (1u128 << 83) - 1, (gf.irr ^ (1u128 << 83)) as u64, a, b) }; } and the same for `sqr`. When `gf.n == 83`, `gf.mask` is `2^83 - 1` by the definition of the mask and `gf.n` is 83, so the arguments are the very values the parent passes; the same function is called with the same arguments, only with `n` and `mask` as constants so the shifts fold into immediates. For every other field the parent's line runs unchanged. A reduced field element is unique, so every product and square is the parent's, and through it the library's. The parent's `fast_field::check` still runs before any use and compares `fmul` and `fsqr` (now the specialised path at n = 83) with the library's `gf.mul` and `gf.sqr` on edge cases and 65,536 pseudo-random pairs, failing closed. The edits are the two insertions, a header comment, the summary's `field_ops_pipeline` (the parent's name plus `+n83_const_reduce_shift`, so a row says which producer ran), and an appended test module `fieldops2_tests` (run by the workflow's `cargo test --bins`): the specialised product against the library's on all 2^20 pairs of a 1,024-element sample, the specialised square against the library's and against the parent's general path on 2^18 elements, and the field it runs on (n = 83, mask 2^83 - 1). Nothing else changes: the proto_r12 candidate (R2) that also touched the linear run finder was rejected and is not here.

primary_choice.primary: end to end (rank stage + cold process), not cold only
primary_choice.why: The headline row is defined by its end-to-end cost, and R1 touches the rank stage as well as the cold process, so a cold-only primary would measure another quantity. The A/A pairs of the k4c400 run (identical work, same seed) put the per-pair noise of an E2E ratio at sd 0.0103 in log (cold 0.0121), so E2E is no noisier than cold; at 12 x 3 pairs the E2E design resolves a 1.010 effect with power 0.998 and 1.005 with 0.668 (cold only: 0.997 and 0.563), while a cold-only schedule would save about 13 min. The saving does not justify changing the estimand. Cold is co-reported as a secondary.

question: Is the END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) of the field-ops-2 producer R1 (ic_online_fieldops2_r770, a constant reduce shift at n = 83) lower than the field-ops producer's (ic_online_fieldops_r770), BOTH on the D4 closure base (K' = 4, 400 orbits), the current headline row's base? The two merged n=83 changes are stacked: only the binary differs between the sides, and the base, header, table, points and rank seeds are the same. Repeated alternating pairs and a 95% two-stage paired bootstrap lower bound above 1 decide (AGENTS.md, 'CPU performance isolation gate', Tier 1).

section_5a.what_is_counted: rho: counted in this run (rT's own charges_setup_and_solve in every rT process). IC: neither producer emits operation counts, so the IC units are a MODEL from the archived counted run 39882571652, applied to THIS run's measured probes and attempts per side. Both sides do identical group-operation work (gated), so the model gives A and B the SAME units: it prices the D4 row against rho at the in-run gap and cannot see a field-arithmetic speed-up. That is a property of the accounting, not a finding

tier_rule: AGENTS.md 'CPU performance evidence tiers', Tier 1: same pinned exposed CPU, same workload and limits; code and workload hashes, paired order, raw failures, correctness, process CPU time, memory, cgroup throttling and memory failures, steal time and scheduling counters recorded; repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound exceeds 1
why_this_run: R1 was measured against the field-ops producer on the M38 base only (1.0256 [1.0236, 1.0278], run 42424680756, mostly index build); D4 was measured against M38 on the field-ops producer only (2.0014 [1.8777, 2.1308], run 42425640847). Ratios from different runs do not compose, and D4 shifts the mix of stages (index build 40% of E2E instead of 55%, self-test on the smaller domain, 4 rank attempts), so the stacked effect is measured, not multiplied. Expected effect is about 2-3% [pcc:unverified]; this is an expectation, not a measurement.
